newsitem.title: UK: Speculative rally in LME copper reverses in rings.
newsitem.headline: Speculative rally in LME copper reverses in rings.

text.p: A fast-moving speculative rally in copper ground to a halt on Thursday afternoon and dealers wagered the metal's upside momentum was spent.
Market talk pinned the rally, which took copper some $50 higher during the pre-market to $2,609 at its peak, to options-related covering and borrowing by a Far East firm.
Prices had gapped higher on Wednesday, gaining some $40 and hitting 13-month highs, and the surge was extended seamlessly on Thursday morning.
But midway through the rings, three months copper came off the boil and eventually settled well off its highs at $2,590 per tonne, which was still a gain of $29 from Wednesday's kerb close.
"It looks like whoever was covering is done covering," a floor trader said. "People sensed that and anyone with some lending or selling to do came in and pushed the price down in almost no volumes."

Another trader said the large Far East firm had to cover upside call options it had granted but it had done a trade-off deal with a large U.S. investment bank outside of the ring, taking the heat out of the market.
An options source said the firm's strategy was to buy nearby in-the-money options and finance them by granting forward out of-the-money calls and puts.
Tightening nearby spreads had helped fuel the rally, with the cash/threes backwardation flaring from around $60 at the start of the week to $110/120 at one point during Thursday's pre-market.
But, like the three months price, the cash/threes backwardation came in by the end of the kerb to $95/$105 -- about $5 easier than on Wednesday afternoon.
On the downside copper has technical support at $2,550.
Shipping problems at Ok Tedi mine in Papua New Guinea could be mildly supportive, but fundamentals were quiet overall ahead of the summer slowdown, traders siad.
The other metals took a back seat to copper and generally were little changed from Wednesday's finish.
"All the action was in copper. And because it would seem to be short covering, there's been little response in the other metals," a trader said.
Aluminium drifted lower to settle at $1,619, down $4. Traders said it probably needed to consolidate in the $1,600-$1,630 range after advancing strongly in the preceding several days.
Zinc came under some pressure following the 2,225-tonne rise in LME stocks and ended $8 lower at $1,360. However, support was seen emerging around $1,355.
Lead shed $1 to end at $636, while tin ws $20 firmer at $5,600.
